findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. Those are mutually exclusive membership roles, so the condition is never true for a normal team admin or owner. Team hosts who are not the booking user and not an attendee are always rejected with FORBIDDEN, so the team path this check was meant to allow cannot add guests.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials after the DB write
findings.body: Attendees are inserted first, then EventManager is built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking host's credentials are loaded on booking.user and never used. When the caller is a team admin or an attendee, the update runs with credentials that do not own the event, so the host calendar/video attendee list is not updated. updateCalendarAttendees is not in a transaction and is not caught; if it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already stored, and sendAddGuestsEmails never runs, so nobody is notified and a retry is treated as a duplicate.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, pending, or past bookings
findings.body: The handler never checks booking.status or endTime before createMany and before sending mail. Any organizer or attendee can add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or PENDING booking. The new mail classes always attach an ICS with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, so people are invited to a meeting that is not an accepted upcoming event. The bookings list also keeps this action on past confirmed rows (bookedActions is rendered when isBookingInPast && isConfirmed), so the UI offers the same flow after the event has ended.

findings.title: Host disableGuests setting is not enforced
findings.body: eventType is loaded but disableGuests is never read. Hosts turn that flag on so bookers cannot invite extra people or forward the meeting link. This mutation still creates attendees and emails them the full invite, including videoCallData (URL and password) when a video reference exists, so the event-type privacy setting is bypassed by anyone who passes the organizer/attendee check.

findings.title: Seated events get extra attendees without seat records
findings.body: If eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot is set, each attendee is a seat holder backed by a BookingSeat. This handler still createMany's Attendee rows and does not create seats or check remaining capacity. Seat counts, no-show, and per-seat cancel flows that use seatsReferences will disagree with booking.attendees. sendAddGuestsEmails also sends every attendee a normal scheduled/add-guests email and never passes seatsShowAttendees, so hidden seat lists are emailed to the new addresses.

findings.title: Guest emails are not normalized, deduped, or blacklist-safe
findings.body: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest is compared with includes(guest) and with attendee.email using raw ===. Zod's email() does not lowercase, so Guest@x.com misses a blacklist entry of guest@x.com and is also treated as a new attendee when guest@x.com is already on the booking. The filter also does not dedupe the input array, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema has no .max() or uniqueness check, so one request can insert repeated rows and fan out an unbounded number of meeting invites. The organizer address is not excluded either.

findings.title: Notification uses the raw guest list, not the inserted guests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is called with the original input, not uniqueGuests. Inside that helper, any attendee whose email is in that list gets AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new confirmed booking invite) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee, or mixing new and old addresses, therefore sends current participants a fresh 'scheduled' ICS while the people who were actually inserted can be classified wrong if casing differs from the stored email.

findings.title: Add-guest mail ignores standard email disable flags
findings.body: Every other sender in this file bails out when event type metadata has disableStandardEmails for the host or attendee. sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee, and the handler never passes eventType.metadata. Event types that disabled standard mail still blast guest-added and scheduled invites, including meeting links, when guests are added.

findings.title: New guests are stored with an empty name
findings.body: createMany sets name to "" and copies the organizer timezone and locale. Attendee mail then builds To as `${name} <${email}>`, which is a blank display name, and the scheduled/add-guest templates greet an empty name. Guests also get times in the host timezone because the dialog never collects theirs.
